approach: Add pure helpers in hestia.rs and call them from `Athena::throughput_review`, ahead of the open-request check. The previous per-stage medians are recomputed from `landed_jobs` cut to the previous review's `landings`, so the record schema does not change. `stage_growth` returns the stages whose median minutes grew, largest first. `throughput_review` always compares and names the grown stages, whether or not a design request is open. When the median is more than `SLOWDOWN_RATIO` (1.25) times the previous review's recorded median, it also queues a `Priority: high` request through `StewardRequest::new` and `self.queue`. That request is built in code and does not use the model, and it names the biggest-growing stage with its measured and previous minutes. The title starts `Throughput slowdown: `, and an open request with that marker suppresses a duplicate. The grown stages go in the review `note` and in a `ui.line`. The design-request path (the model, the single open-request rule, `throughput_due`, the 20% trigger) is unchanged. A small refactor in status.rs exposes the per-stage median computation so the review and `Throughput::compute` share one definition. Tests are added in the hestia.rs test module, reusing `seed_landed`, `timed_job`, `earlier_review`, `athena_with`, `Lines` and `put`.

decisions.choice: Recompute the previous per-stage medians from `landed_jobs(records)`: take the first `previous.landings` jobs (landed-at order) and, of those, the newest THROUGHPUT_WINDOW, then take the median per stage. Compare these with `measured.median_stages`. The median-grew test uses the recorded `previous.window_median_minutes`.
decisions.reason: The review record stores only the total median and the landing count (records.rs ~2174). This needs no schema change, and `landed_jobs` already sorts jobs by landed-at, so the previous window is the one the previous review saw. The brief's 'small' default asks for exactly this.

rejected.option: Add a per-stage-medians field to `ThroughputReview` (and its JSON schema and round-trip test)
rejected.why: It needs a schema bump (`deny_unknown_fields`, `THROUGHPUT_REVIEW_SCHEMA`) and does nothing for old records. The recompute gives the same answer.

rejected.option: Cut the previous window by `landed_at <= previous.at`
rejected.why: A job's landing record can be written after a review that already counted it (`landing_end` takes the later of outcome and record), so a time cut can disagree with `previous.landings`. The count cut matches the basis the record stored.

decisions.choice: Queue the slowdown request from code, with `StewardRequest::new(Some(Priority::High), ...)` and `self.queue`. Do it before and regardless of the open design request check, and never ask the model for it.
decisions.reason: The failure was a slowdown hidden behind an open request. A deterministic rule that tests can drive without the model is the mechanism the 'mechanism' default asks for. `StewardRequest::new` checks the text against the plan parse, so `athena plan` accepts it.

rejected.option: Ask the model to describe the slowdown
rejected.why: It is non-deterministic and it costs money. The brief asks for the measured stage and minutes, which the code already has.

rejected.option: Lift the open-request guard for design requests
rejected.why: It would queue a second design proposal. The brief and criterion 5 keep that behavior.

decisions.choice: The slowdown request text does not contain the review's id.
decisions.reason: `throughput_followups` treats any landed job whose request text contains a reviewing id as the change that implements that review's proposal (hestia.rs ~1392). If the slowdown request cited the id, its landing would falsely close the prediction made in the same review.

rejected.option: Cite the review id like the design request does
rejected.why: It would corrupt the follow-up measurement for a review that also queued a design proposal.

decisions.choice: Dedupe with a distinct marker `SLOWDOWN_MARKER = "Throughput slowdown: "`. Generalise `open_throughput_request` into a private `open_request_with_marker(records, marker)` that it calls with `THROUGHPUT_MARKER`. A slowdown suppresses another slowdown only, never a design request.
decisions.reason: The two kinds of request are independent. The design marker is `Throughput design: `, so neither title is a prefix of the other. The stage naming still runs when the request is suppressed.

rejected.why: An open design request would then suppress the slowdown request, which is the bug.

decisions.choice: `SLOWDOWN_RATIO = 1.25` with a strict `>`. `is_slowdown(previous, current)` is false when previous is not above 0. The existing `WORSEN_RATIO` (1.2) stays as the trigger.
decisions.reason: This matches `throughput_due`'s 'exactly 20% is not more than 20%' style. A review between 20% and 25% still runs and names stages but queues nothing.

rejected.why: The brief puts the 20% trigger out of scope.

decisions.choice: The stage with the largest added minutes (current minus previous median) is the 'grew most'. Ties keep pipeline order. Growth below 1e-6 minutes is ignored. If the median grew over 25% but no stage median grew, queue nothing and say so in the note.
decisions.reason: Medians of totals and medians of stages are not additive, so the case can occur. A request must name a stage, and inventing one would be wrong.

rejected.option: Fall back to the stage with the largest current median
rejected.why: It would name a stage that did not grow, which contradicts the criterion.

decisions.choice: Carry the finding in the existing `note` string and a `ui.line` printed from `throughput_review`, as the follow-up lines already are. The record gains no field, and the note text is appended after any existing note.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert `note.contains("still open")` and `starts_with("no proposal")`, so appending keeps them true. No schema change.

rejected.why: It needs a schema change. The note names the job, and the queued request carries the detail.

decisions.choice: Extract the per-stage median computation in `Throughput::compute` (status.rs ~905-915) into `StageMinutes::median_of(window: &[LandedJob])`. Both `compute` and the review call it.
decisions.reason: One definition of 'median stage minutes' means the review compares like with like, and `compute`'s output does not change.

rejected.why: The two definitions could drift apart, and the comparison would then be wrong without any test failing.

decisions.choice: records.rs gets a doc-comment-only change (the `note` field's doc, the `Worsened` doc). It has no field, schema or validation change.
decisions.reason: The brief lists records.rs as a deliverable, and the doc should say the note can hold a slowdown remark. The code does not need more.

rejected.why: The `note` doc would then describe only proposal-less reasons.

If growth is non-empty, build a remark such as `median {prev:.1} to {now:.1} min; stages that grew: producer 25.0 to 45.0, checks 0.0 to 10.0`. If `slowdown` and growth is non-empty and no `open_request_with_marker(&records, SLOWDOWN_MARKER)` is open, call `slowdown_request` and `self.queue`, and add the job id to the remark (or the error text if building or queuing fails, as the design branch does). If `slowdown` and the request is already open, say so (`slowdown request {id} is still open`). If `slowdown` and growth is empty, say that the median grew over 25% but no stage's median did. This runs before the existing `if let Some(open) = open_throughput_request` branch, which stays as it is. At the end append the remark to `note` (joined with `; ` when `note` is not empty, so `starts_with("no proposal")` and `contains("still open")` still hold). risks.risk: The reconstructed previous per-stage medians differ slightly from what the previous review saw.
risks.mitigation: The cut by `previous.landings` is an approximation when some landed jobs are unmeasured or their order shifted, because `landed_jobs` leaves out landed jobs that ran no model. The comparison is only a growth ranking, so the effect is bounded. The doc comment says it is a reconstruction. If the previous window cannot be derived (empty), no stages are named and no request is queued, which the note says. The 25% decision uses the recorded median, not the reconstruction.

risks.risk: The median of totals can exceed 1.25 times the previous one while no stage median grew, so no request names a stage.
risks.mitigation: The case is rare. The note says the median grew but no stage's median did, and queues nothing. The doc comment and a test of `stage_growth` with such inputs state the behavior. The alternative of naming a stage that did not grow was rejected.

risks.risk: A slowdown request is queued on every review while the slowdown persists.
risks.mitigation: A distinct marker suppresses another slowdown while one is open, and each comparison is against the previous review, so a steady slowdown is flagged once. Test 1 covers the suppressed second review.

risks.risk: The slowdown request could be mistaken for the change that implements a design proposal made in the same review.
risks.mitigation: The request text omits the review id and a test asserts it. That keeps `throughput_followups` from treating the landing of the slowdown request as the cited change.

risks.risk: `athena plan` refuses the new request, or the admission scan rejects it.
risks.mitigation: The slowdown request goes through `StewardRequest::new`, which checks acceptance and files against the plan parse and applies boundary rewording. The body keeps stage lists on one line with no bullet-like lines. The pure test checks `request_text_acceptance`, and `queue` runs `refuse_banned_input`.

risks.risk: The test's median does not reach 60 because the window mixes old and new jobs.
risks.mitigation: Pick fixtures where the 20-job window flips: ten old jobs then 11 new ones make the window median equal the new value (9 old, 11 new). The test asserts `review.window_median_minutes` equals 60.0 (and 24.5, 25.5) before the other assertions.
